en: The Apadāna of the Elder Kilañjadāyaka Udakāsanavagga, Chapter 4 I was once a weaver in the city of Benares, And I wove a mat of reeds for the sake of the Buddha. Having offered it with a devout heart, I attained the fruit of stream-entry. For eighty-four thousand aeons I never fell into the lower realms; I enjoyed celestial pleasures In the heavenly worlds. When my lifespan here was exhausted, I was reborn among humans; For eighty-four thousand births I was always a king of men. In every birth I took, I was born into a noble family; I possessed great wealth and power, And was honored by the world. Through the merit of that deed, I have now reached this final birth; I am now a monk of great wisdom, A disciple of the Tathāgata. By the power of that gift, I have attained the fruit of Arhatship; My mind is liberated from all taints, Cool and peaceful, free from suffering. This is the true account of the Elder Kilañjadāyaka, Recited in the Udakāsanavagga.
“In the delightful city of Tivarā,
I was then a reed-worker;
when Siddhattha was the lamp of the world, ...”
The people there were full of faith;
for the purpose of honoring the Lord of the World,
they sought out palm leaves.
While they were making offerings to the Buddha,
I gave them a palm-leaf fan.
Ninety-four aeons ago,
Whatever deed I performed then,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of that reed mat.
In the seventy-seventh aeon,
I was King Jaladdhara,
endowed with the seven treasures.
A wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Kilañjadāyaka recited these verses.
This is the fourth legend of the elder Kilañjadāyaka.
